ei.subject: 영어

fullPassage: Managers frequently try to play psychologist, to "figure out" why an employee has acted in a certain way. Empathizing with employees in order to understand their point of view can be very helpful. However, when dealing with a problem area, in particular, remember that it is not the person who is bad, but the actions exhibited on the job. Avoid making suggestions to employees about personal traits they should change; instead suggest more acceptable ways of performing. For example, instead of focusing on a person's "unreliability," a manager might focus on the fact that the employee "has been late to work seven times this month." It is difficult for employees to change who they are; it is usually much easier for them to change how they act.

questions.passage: Managers ①<u>frequently</u> try to play psychologist, to "figure out" why an employee has acted in a certain way. ②<u>Empathizing</u> with employees in order to understand their point of view can be very helpful. However, when dealing with a problem area, in particular, remember that it is not the person who is bad, but the actions ③<u>exhibiting</u> on the job. Avoid making suggestions to employees about personal traits they should change; instead suggest more acceptable ways of performing. For example, instead of focusing on a person's "unreliability," a manager might focus on the fact that the employee "has been late to work seven times this month." It is difficult for employees to change who they are; it is usually much ④<u>easier</u> for them to change how they act.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: exhibiting → exhibited: actions는 수동으로 '보여지는' 것이므로 과거분사 사용
det.analysis:
❌ ① frequently: 빈도부사가 동사 try 앞에 올바르게 위치
❌ ② Empathizing: 동명사 주어 — Empathizing ... can be very helpful
✅ ③ exhibiting → exhibited: actions는 '보여지는' 것이므로 수동의 과거분사 exhibited가 올바름
❌ ④ easier: 비교급 — much easier for them
det.tip: 분사의 능동(-ing)/수동(-ed): 행동이 '보여지는' 것이므로 수동(exhibited)이 맞습니다.

questions.passage: Managers frequently try to play psychologist, to "figure out" ①<u>what</u> an employee has acted in a certain way. Avoid ③<u>making</u> suggestions to employees about personal traits they should change; instead suggest more acceptable ways of performing. For example, instead of ④<u>focusing</u> on a person's "unreliability," a manager might focus on the fact that the employee "has been late to work seven times this month." It is difficult for employees to change who they are; it is usually much easier for them to change how they act.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: what → why: figure out 뒤 이유를 묻는 간접의문문에는 why 사용
det.analysis:
✅ ① what → why: 'figure out' 뒤에 이유를 묻는 간접의문문이므로 why가 올바름. what은 의미 부적절
❌ ② helpful: 보어 형용사 — can be very helpful
❌ ③ making: Avoid 뒤 동명사 — Avoid making suggestions
❌ ④ focusing: 전치사 of 뒤 동명사 — instead of focusing
det.tip: 'figure out why ~'는 '왜 ~인지 알아내다'입니다. 의문사 선택에 주의하세요.

However, when dealing with a problem area, in particular, remember that it is not the person who is ②<u>bad</u>, but the actions exhibited on the job. Avoid making suggestions to employees about personal traits they should change; instead ④<u>suggesting</u> more ③<u>acceptable</u> ways of performing. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: suggesting → suggest: 세미콜론 뒤 instead와 함께 명령문이므로 동사원형 사용
det.analysis:
❌ ① acted: 현재완료의 과거분사 — has acted in a certain way
❌ ② bad: 보어 형용사 — the person who is bad
❌ ③ acceptable: 형용사로 ways 수식 — more acceptable ways
✅ ④ suggesting → suggest: 세미콜론 뒤 명령문 구조이므로 동사원형 suggest가 올바름
det.tip: 세미콜론(;) 뒤 'instead'가 오면 명령문 구조로 동사원형을 씁니다.

questions.passage: Managers frequently try to play psychologist, to "figure out" why an employee has acted in a certain way. Avoid making suggestions to employees about personal traits they should change; instead suggest more ③<u>acceptable</u> ways of performing. For example, instead of focusing on a person's "unreliability," a manager might focus on the fact that the employee "has been late to work seven times this month." It is ④<u>difficult</u> for employees to change who they are; it is usually much easier for them to change how they act.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 직원들의 관점을 이해하기 위해 공감한다. 나쁜 것은 사람이 아니라 행동이다. 더 바람직한 업무 방식을 제안하라. 자신을 바꾸는 것은 어렵다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① understand: 관점을 '이해하다'는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② good → bad: 문제는 사람이 아니라 행동이라는 문맥에서 'bad'가 적절. 'good'은 반대 의미
❌ ③ acceptable: '바람직한' 방식이라는 문맥에 적절
❌ ④ difficult: 자신을 바꾸기 '어렵다'는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 'not A but B' 구문의 맥락을 파악하세요. A(사람)가 나쁜 게 아니라 B(행동)가 나쁜 것입니다.

questions.passage: Managers frequently try to play psychologist, to "figure out" why an employee has acted in a certain way. Empathizing with employees in order to understand their point of view can be very ①<u>harmful</u>. However, when dealing with a problem area, in particular, remember that it is not the person who is bad, but the actions exhibited on the job. ②<u>Avoid</u> making suggestions to employees about personal traits they should ③<u>change</u>; instead suggest more acceptable ways of performing. For example, instead of focusing on a person's "unreliability," a manager might focus on the fact that the employee "has been late to work seven times this month." It is difficult for employees to change who they are; it is usually much ④<u>easier</u> for them to change how they act.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 공감은 해로울 수 있다? 아니다. 공감은 매우 도움이 될 수 있다. 개인적 특성에 대한 제안을 피하라. 행동 변화가 더 쉽다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① harmful → helpful: 공감이 '도움이 된다(helpful)'는 긍정적 문맥이므로 'harmful(해로운)'은 반대 의미
❌ ② Avoid: 개인적 특성 제안을 '피하라'는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ change: 특성을 '바꿔야 한다'는 문맥에 적절
❌ ④ easier: 행동 변화가 '더 쉽다'는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 긍정적 맥락(공감의 가치)에서 'harmful'과 'helpful'의 의미 대비를 파악하세요.

However, when dealing with a problem area, in particular, remember that it is not the person who is bad, but the actions exhibited on the job. Avoid making suggestions to employees about personal traits they should change; instead suggest more acceptable ways of __________. For example, instead of focusing on a person's "unreliability," a manager might focus on the fact that the employee "has been late to work seven times this month." It is difficult for employees to change who they are; it is usually much easier for them to change how they act.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 대신 더 바람직한 업무 수행 방식을 제안하라.
det.analysis:
❌ ① dealing: '다루는' 방식은 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ② empathizing: '공감하는' 방식은 제안 대상이 아님
✅ ③ performing: 'ways of ____'에서 '업무 수행' 방식을 의미
❌ ④ acting: '행동하는'은 마지막 문장의 내용이며 이 위치의 원문과 다름
det.tip: 'suggest more acceptable ways of ____'에서 개인적 특성 대비 '업무 수행 방식'이 대조됩니다.

❌ ③ certain: '특정한'은 의미가 모호함
❌ ④ acceptable: '수용할 만한'은 부정적 맥락의 actions와 맞지 않음

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

❌ ③ 본문은 정체성 변화가 어렵고 행동 변화가 쉽다고 함 — 반대

관리자는 직원의 심리를 분석하는 것을 완전히 피해야 한다.

questions.passage: Managers frequently try to play psychologist, to "figure out" why an employee has acted in a certain way. Empathizing with employees in order to understand their point of view can be very helpful. However, when dealing with a problem area, in particular, remember that it is not the person who is bad, but the actions exhibited on the job. Avoid making suggestions to employees about personal traits <u>they should change</u>; instead suggest more acceptable ways of performing. For example, instead of focusing on a person's "unreliability," a manager might focus on the fact that the employee "has been late to work seven times this month." It is difficult for employees to change who they are; it is usually much easier for them to change how they act.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>they</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

✅ ③ 'suggestions to employees about personal traits they should change'에서 they = employees(직원들)
❌ ④ 특성은 사물이므로 they로 지칭하기 부적절
det.tip: 'employees about personal traits they should change'에서 they의 선행사를 찾으세요.
